meanings: carrying forward, going on; the carrying on (of a work, of a book)
derivation: ser 'go on, carry forward' + -Ol (verbal noun, slender -yl), as kethyl; the folk etymology of Seren's name heard in it (orrowen_v2 §4.6); unit S04 (II.3, 'carry this Book on after us')

meanings: Brenn of the Outpost: the man who picked up the stone (IV.3)
derivation: the epithet construct: Brenn + S·deldvar 'an outpost' (d > r), as Corlen Dhavow (S·tavow); names are names, the epithet is a place; unit S04 (IV.3)

meanings: the Kneeling Guest ('the guest who knelt'): the same row as unit W01's O-W01-01, with IV.4's et arra for the Guest; kept here so this unit validates alone
derivation: a phrase: et the + arra 'a guest' + sa REL(+S) + re PST(+S) + lumm 'kneel' (l unchanged), as Voss sa re vess; as a possessor it keeps its article (ternil et arra sa re lumm, the Kneeling Guest's rite), as hosk et ganna; unit S04 (IV.3), after W01

meanings: the right hand ('the true hand'); right (of the hand, the arm)
derivation: a phrase: garl 'a hand' + venn 'true' (the lexicon renders the Book's 'right' by venn); its fellow is garl ullen, the left; also sestyarl venn, the right arm; unit S04 (II.3, IV.3)

meanings: the left hand ('the other hand'); left (of the hand)
derivation: a phrase: garl 'a hand' + ullen 'other; left (the other hand)'; its fellow is garl venn; unit S04 (II.3, IV.3)

meanings: the Aetherbonded ('those of the mortar of the sky'): the full name, beside et Lodhan, the Bonded
derivation: the construct: Lodhan 'the Bonded' + S·helv 'the sky' (h unchanged), built as the canon's Lodh Helv 'the Aetherbond'; like every construct head it takes no article; unit S04 (II.3)

meanings: a paragraph each; paragraph by paragraph ('course and course')
derivation: a phrase: trenn 'a course; a line; a paragraph' + eth + trenn, as hos eth hos 'one by one' (pilot I.1); after hos eth ullen 'by turns' (pilot IV.4) it gives the headnotes' 'by turns, a paragraph each'; unit S04

meanings: two by two; in pairs ('two and two')
derivation: a phrase: pa 'two' + eth + pa, as hos eth hos 'one by one'; pa stands without its noun, so nothing softens; unit S04 (II.3, the Theoliths)

orrowen: Cadhan o hosen re yal cadhat lona
meanings: This we (two) lay as it was laid for us (two): the hearth's closing formula as a bonded pair says it
derivation: a phrase: Cadhan lay-1DU + o it(+S) + hosen as + re PST(+S) + yal S·be.PST + cadhat laid + lona at-1DU; the formula Cadhar o hosen re yal cadhat lor in the dual, because 'where the Book gives Halyna a plural verb, the Orrowen original is dual' (orrowen_v2 §3.9 item 1), as pilot I.1 put it in the singular for Kael (Cadhom … lom); unit S04 (II.3, IV.3)

meanings: grow up, come of age ('grow to the height')
derivation: a phrase: tev 'grow, sprout' + dem until(+N) + susk 'the height' (s unchanged), as dem susk 'up'; unit S04 (II.3, 'when bonded children come of age')

meanings: by heart ('from the heart')
derivation: a phrase: hy from(+S) + S·molt 'a heart' (m > v); unit S04 (IV.3, 'I can say it by heart')

meanings: a season, a short while ('a small time')
derivation: a phrase: fedh 'a time, a season' + lyss 'small'; said where hos fedh, 'one time', would be heard as 'once'; unit S04 (II.3, 'for a season')

meanings: does not …? did not …? (the negative question: Q + NEG)
derivation: a phrase: ho Q(+S) + nath NEG(+N); ho's softening falls on nath, which does not change, and nath beds the verb (ho nath senn); built as nath re (pilot I.1, G1), the particle that governs the verb standing next to it. A grammar proposal: the spec gives the question and the negative apart; unit S04 (II.3, 'does not the right one die too?')

meanings: the killing blow ('the stroke of killing')
derivation: the construct: drunn 'a mallet; strike, a blow' + S·hurrol 'killing' (h unchanged); after dem the bedding leaves dr- as it is (§2.5: a nasalised d before r stays d); unit S04 (IV.3, 'he screamed for the killing blow')

meanings: the Fall (of the havens) ('the falling')
derivation: the article + ommol 'falling', the verbal noun of omm 'fall'; hy et Ommol 'since the Fall'; unit S04 (II.3)

orrowen: Uld sa lumm lo tho yebb, ul vimm tho hrisur
meanings: one who kneels at your door is under your roof: the guest-law (arraharal), 'no older law among any people' (IV.3)
derivation: a verbless saying, as the proverbs are (Grest um hos, grest um vana): uld 'a man' + sa REL(+S) + lumm 'kneel' + lo at(+S) + tho your(+S) + S·gebb 'a door' (g > y) + ul vimm 'under' + tho + S·crisur 'a roof' (c > h); the singular tho, as the law is said to each host; unit S04 (IV.3)

orrowen: Besk nasesket. Dask bynden. Hesset. Sceth vorrat eth luskat.
meanings: the warden's report (IV.3): 'Unknown intruder. Hostile intent. Neutralized. Vessel burned and released.'
derivation: four verbless namings, as a clerk's register sets them down: besk 'a stranger, an intruder' + nasesket 'unknown'; dask 'an end, an intent' + bynden 'hostile'; hesset 'stopped' (the participle of hess, the Guest's own first word); sceth 'a hull, a vessel' + vorrat 'burned' + eth + luskat 'released'; unit S04 (IV.3)

meanings: (Y) is N years old: 'N years are at Y' (Re yal rostnoth surr lom, 'I was nineteen')
